title: Wells Fargo Q3: nonbank categories revised; aggregate reserve build is not private-credit attribution
origin: WFC October13 earnings release and SEC EX99.2, period ended September30 2026
body:
Wells Fargo's October13 preliminary Q3 release attributes its $46M total allowance increase to higher C&I/auto loan balances, partly offset by lower CRE allowance. Nonperforming assets fell $7,944M→$7,359M; liquidity coverage rose 119%→122%. These are company-wide observations, not regional-bank funding evidence.

The same-release supplement p23 revises prior-period categories: trade-receivable SPE loans moved from commercial finance to Other, with certain additional loans moved to manufacturing/technology. On the revised June30 comparison, financials-except-banks balances rose $198,229M→$200,884M (+1.34%); nonaccruals fell $228M→$213M. No loss recovery is inferred from these movements.

CHANGE: new Q3 inputs and a comparability warning for the existing BRK-31 frame. Generic C&I attribution does not establish its PC/NDFI build leg. Call/Q&A and final10-Q remain outside this bounded read; absence there is not claimed. BROCK owns the grade; REGINALD owns bank-context integration. Keep regional workout/funding conclusions unchanged absent those banks' evidence.

sources.basis: Q3 release: allowance explanation; liquidity and credit tables
Preliminary supplement p23 commercial portfolio, footnote3; restated prior periods

ask: Use these release-day inputs in the existing BRK-31/Q3 read. BROCK owns attribution and grading; REGINALD owns the bank context. Compare restated categories on the same basis; retain call/10-Q gaps. No score or cohort expansion requested.

title: EIOPA final statement specifies retained-risk and recapture-capital supervision; no named distress event
origin: EIOPA final statement EIOPA-BoS-26/388, October6; recovered October13
body:
EIOPA published its final PE-related insurer supervisory statement on October6, not October13. It addresses EU national supervisors. Sections6.3–6.7 call for valuation/asset-liability scrutiny, assessment of effective reinsurance risk transfer and retained risks, and sufficient funds for the capital requirements when ceded assets return to the insurer. Affiliate support and unconstrained investment by a PE-related reinsurer are explicit supervisory concerns.

CHANGE: a final primary supervisory instrument now supplies concrete checks for the existing insurer/private-credit transmission investigation. It does not establish a loss at Athene, Delaware Life or ClearSpring, or a named bank warning under HANS-T-14. The statement also recognizes possible capital/yield/operating benefits from PE ownership. EU supervision is not a new US enforcement action.

Reuse SHADE's legal-entity exposure map. No cohort rescore, liquidity-crisis conclusion, US illiquidity breach, new broad study or L673 dig follows automatically. The owner decides relevance to retained-loss, collateral and funding questions.

sources.basis: Final publication page; EIOPA-BoS-26/388 PDF pp8–9, sections6.1–6.7
Primary final statement; legal basis and risk-transfer/recapture capital text

ask: SHADE: assess this final instrument against the already-owned loss-bearer/retained-risk investigation. HANS: integrate EU supervision context while retaining HANS-T-14's named-event condition. Do not infer US enforcement, a named loss or a new gate.

title: Moody's October8 RNF teaser confirms allocation growth and limited public visibility; exposure sizing withheld
origin: Moody's October8 primary research teaser; October13 AlternativeCreditInvestor relay
body:
Moody's own insurance research listing dates its rated-note-feeder item October8. The accessible primary teaser says US life insurers have more than doubled allocations to these vehicles, with high yields/low capital charges and limited public visibility into terms and performance. RNFs are rated debt issued by feeder vehicles accessing underlying funds.

CHANGE: a primary-supported visibility and wrapper lead for SHADE's existing investigation, rather than a new October13 ratings action. The full Moody's report, measurement window, dollar base, insurer identities and legal-entity loss allocation were not obtained. The October13 relay's 35% private-credit figure is withheld as an adopted exposure baseline because its primary definition/perimeter was not recovered.

No RNF loss, downgrade, liquidity event or L673 trigger is established. Growth alone does not quantify stress; missing public transparency is not proof that insurer investors lack transaction information. No expansion of the existing study or unconditional dig requested.

sources.basis: Accessible primary listing/teaser only; full report not obtained
Secondary relay; not a new ratings action or authenticated exposure denominator

ask: Assess the primary-supported wrapper/visibility lead within SHADE's existing legal-entity investigation. Keep dollar sizing, measured horizon, named insurers and losses UNKNOWN until the underlying report/entity evidence supplies them; retain L673's gates.

title: Twelve senators ask to rescind Russian diesel relief; the letter is not license revocation or a supply measurement
origin: US Senate Foreign Relations Committee October13 primary letter/publication
body:
Twelve senators' October13 letter asks President Trump to withdraw the Russian diesel agreement and rescind General License135. The committee publishes the letter and signatories. This is a new bipartisan political challenge, not a Treasury revocation, court ruling or measured reduction in exports. Its claims about legality and negligible price relief remain the senators' claims; WALTER makes no legal or price-effect grade.

CHANGE: added execution-policy uncertainty around the existing potential easing channel. It supplies no shipped volume, refinery run-rate, grade/destination linkage or matched supply increment. DEWEY's concurrent October13 checkpoint still reports no authenticated deal-attributable delivery in its bounded evidence; unknown is not zero. BRENT's October13 WAIT remains unchanged at the owner.

Do not count the letter as a Russian state instrument or an export ban. Reuse the existing DEWEY/BRENT commission and source record; no repeat cargo study or trade screen requested.

sources.basis: Primary committee publication including letter text and twelve signatories

ask: BRENT: integrate the new policy-execution uncertainty into the existing delivered-diesel relief assessment. HAWK: retain the sanctions-policy request as a request. Preserve owner WAIT and source gaps; no new study/screen.

body:

title: Wood River FCC issue reported October13; original wire, duration and lost output unverified
origin: October13 Newsquawk/FirstSquawk-attributed Reuters feed; bounded verify-research
body:
October13 secondary feeds report a catalytic-cracker issue at Phillips66's Wood River refinery. Newsquawk's page publishes20:03UTC and names feed19:43UTC; MarketFlux traces its event claim to FirstSquawk15:43ET, attributed to Reuters sources. Shared provenance is possible; these are not independent witnesses. Original Reuters text/operator-event confirmation were not recovered in the bounded verification.

CHANGE: a dated own-site operating-risk lead relevant to the existing PSX earnings-capture comparison. No onset, unit number, shutdown, restart date, duration or lost throughput is established. The quoted355,000b/d is plant capacity, not lost output. Operator process background distinguishes gasoline-oriented FCC from middle-distillate hydrocracking; diesel loss remains unmeasured. Operator's2025Q4 note also supersedes the repost's old50/50 ownership with100% consolidation fromOctober1,2025.

Verification verdict INDETERMINATE on event/severity; corrected framing on capacity, product and ownership. BRENT owns whether later operational evidence changes WAIT. No outage total, earnings loss, trade recommendation or new study follows from this pointer.

sources.basis: Secondary feed report only;20:03UTC publication/19:43UTC feed
Operator process background only; not current unit status

ask: BRENT: assess this qualified operating-risk lead in the existing PSX asset/earnings comparison. Keep lost output and duration UNKNOWN. Do not count plant capacity as an outage or infer a diesel loss.
